segments.speaker: S1
segments.text: Remote work should be the default for software teams. People are more productive when they control their environment.

segments.speaker: S2
segments.text: I disagree. Teams lose the informal conversations where most real problem solving happens.

segments.speaker: S1
segments.text: Studies of focused tasks show fewer interruptions at home, and fewer interruptions means more output.

segments.speaker: S2
segments.text: So you are saying people should never meet and just sit alone forever? That would destroy any company culture.

segments.speaker: S1
segments.text: That is not what I said. I said remote should be the default, not the only option.

segments.speaker: S2
segments.text: Well, every successful company I know brings people back to the office, so the office must be better.

segments.speaker: S1
segments.text: Those companies also have expensive office leases to justify. And you only know a handful of companies.

segments.speaker: S2
segments.text: You only say this because you hate commuting.

segments.speaker: S1
segments.text: Whether I like commuting has nothing to do with whether the argument is sound.

segments.speaker: S2
segments.text: Fine. But onboarding a junior developer remotely is clearly slower. They learn by watching seniors.

segments.speaker: S1
segments.text: That is a fair point. Maybe juniors need a hybrid period, then remote by default.

fallacies.name: Straw man
fallacies.explanation: S2 restates S1's 'remote as default' as 'never meet and sit alone forever', an extreme distortion, then attacks that extreme for destroying culture instead of the actual proposal.
fallacies.quote: So you are saying people should never meet and just sit alone forever?

fallacies.name: Appeal to popularity
fallacies.explanation: S2 argues the office must be better because every successful company he knows does it, assuming common practice proves superiority, which does not follow.
fallacies.quote: every successful company I know brings people back to the office, so the office must be better.

fallacies.name: Ad hominem (circumstantial)
fallacies.explanation: S2 dismisses S1's argument by citing motive – hating commuting – rather than addressing the evidence. The hidden premise that motive makes the claim false fails.
fallacies.quote: You only say this because you hate commuting.
